# H3 Long Take
**Noncoder edition** · youtube.com/@noncoderr

This workflow turns a written scene and a few reference pictures into an AI video with sound. You write the scene on a timeline, press Run, and pick your favorite take.

## Your first render
1. Install the three custom nodes and download the models. The **Engine** note at the bottom lists every file and where it goes.
2. Press **2** to jump to the Scene editor. Click the first segment, fill in the bracketed prompt, and drop your reference pictures onto it.
3. Press **3** and give your project a name.
4. Press **Run**. Frames appear in Live preview (key **4**) while it works.
5. Press **5** to see your takes. Keep the best one and press **Combine**. The finished video shows up in Save (key **6**).

Keys **1** to **6** jump between the numbered areas. Every area has a side note like this one, so read the note next to wherever you're stuck.

## Three habits that save the most time
**Change one thing per render.** If you change three things and the take improves, you won't know which one helped.

**Run it again before you rewrite anything.** H3 is random from take to take. A bad take is often bad luck, and a new seed fixes it for free.

**Close beats wide.** Faces only look real when they fill a good part of the frame. Start with medium shots and close-ups.

## Where to learn more
The full walkthrough of this workflow is on the Noncoder YouTube channel.
nodes.title: Start here

widgets_values:
# Render settings

## Single or dual
**Single** renders each segment once at full size. Use it for long takes built from Context segments, because the joins stay clean.

**Dual** renders small first, then upscales and sharpens in a second pass. Use it for separate shots. `upscale_by` sets how much bigger the second pass gets, and 1.3 is a safe start.

Leave `sampling_plan` on **custom**. That tells the node to use the green Steps box.

## Steps (green box)
Use **8** for most scenes: dancing, fast hands, busy backgrounds, walking and talking.

Drop to **6** for a talking head, a slow walk, or a locked-off camera.

Use **4** only when nobody speaks. At 4 steps, dialogue loses syllables.

## Takes and seeds
`project_save` on **new** keeps every render as a separate take. **override** replaces the last one.

`seed` on **randomize** gives a fresh take on every Run.

To tweak a take you like, drag its MP4 back onto ComfyUI. That reopens the exact seed and settings. Switch the seed to **fixed**, then change one thing.

To redo a single segment, set `segment_start_number` to its number and `segment_count` to 1.

## How long will it take?
Render time grows in a straight line with pixels, frames and steps. Double any one of them and you roughly double the wait.

Test at 5 seconds and 1 MP before you go longer or bigger.

## Running out of memory?
Switch on **Low-VRAM mode** above. It trades speed for memory. If you still run out, set `enabled_tiling` to true in Render settings.
nodes.title: Render settings, explained

widgets_values:
# Takes

Every Run adds a new take for each segment, and nothing gets overwritten.

## Pick a take
Tick two takes of the same segment to play them side by side, in sync. Keep the better one and untick the other.

When every segment has the take you want, press **Combine**.

## When to throw a take away
**It cuts to another angle partway through.** This is random, so run it again with a new seed.

**The lips look out of sync.** First check that the face stays on screen the whole time. Most bad lip-sync is a hidden cut, not a sync problem.

**The character stares into the lens.** Give them a place to look in every action of the prompt.

**The sound goes dead in the last second.** H3 sometimes does this at the end of a clip. End the action a moment early, or trim it in your editor.
nodes.title: Picking takes

widgets_values:
# Writing a scene that works

## The timeline
Each block on the **Shots** track is one segment, and each segment renders as its own clip. Drag a block's edges to change its length.

Five seconds is the sweet spot. Eight seconds works too, but it takes about half again as long to render.

**Shot** starts a fresh camera setup. **Context** picks up from the end of the previous clip, so motion and sound carry across the join.

## Write every prompt in this order
1. **Name every reference.** "Reference 1 is her face. Reference 2 is her outfit." A picture without a name makes the character drift.
2. **Say where the camera is.** "Medium shot at her car door, camera at chest height."
3. **Give one action every two seconds.** A five-second clip holds about three actions. Cram in more and they blur together.
4. **Describe who they are and what they wear.**
5. **Name two or three ordinary things in the background,** like a delivery van or a bus stop. Plain objects stop the glossy AI look.
6. **Finish with the sound.**

This workflow has no negative prompt. Say what you want instead of what you don't: "an empty street," not "no people."

## Reference pictures
- **Crop the face picture to head and hair** when another picture shows the outfit. Otherwise the clothes in the face picture win.
- **Pair a close picture with a wide one.** A chest-up picture alone says nothing about arm length, and arms come out short.
- **Fill the slots in order,** with no gaps.
- **A wide location picture pulls the camera wide.** Put your camera sentence first and add "the camera is much closer than in Reference 3."
- **Outfit colors leak into crowds** and create lookalikes. Use a crowd picture without your character's color.

## Eyes and faces
A front-facing portrait makes the character stare at the lens for the whole clip. Give one place to look in each action, in screen directions: "she glances screen-left at the road, then over her shoulder." Add "her eyes move before her head."

## Context segments
- Open the prompt with the continuation: same pace, same camera, same light, and no new scenery.
- Still write out the full action. One-line Context prompts get ignored, and the model picks a new camera.
- A Context clip lands about 0.92 seconds early. Write T + 0.92 to hit T.
- Put joins mid-walk, never in a doorway, and never in the middle of a camera move.

## Your own voice
Drop an MP3 on the **Voice** track and click the track's lock. The character speaks your audio. Split segments between sentences, not in the middle of a word.
nodes.title: Writing a scene that works

widgets_values:
# Live preview

Frames appear here while each segment renders. They're rough on purpose. This is a quick sketch of the clip, not the final quality.

## Stop early when you see a problem
Cancelling a bad render saves the rest of its time. Watch for these three:

**The camera is in the wrong place.** Rewrite the camera sentence in the prompt and put it first.

**The face is tiny.** Move the camera closer in the prompt. A face drawn small stays soft, and more resolution won't fix it.

**The shot cuts to a different angle partway through.** H3 does this at random. Rewriting the prompt won't stop it. Run again with a new seed.
nodes.title: What to watch for

widgets_values:
# Save

The finished video lands in `ComfyUI/output/easy_media/projects/<your project name>/out/`.

The MP4 carries the full workflow that made it. Drag it back onto ComfyUI any time to reopen those exact settings.

## Before you post
Watch the whole video once at full size. The preview hides small faces and soft details.

Uploading to YouTube? Upscale to 4K first. YouTube streams 4K uploads at higher quality, even when the original was smaller.

# Engine

You don't need to touch anything here to get a good render. This note lists what the Engine needs.

The small folded **Set** and **Get** nodes carry connections between areas, so no wires cross the canvas. Leave them where they are.

## Which GPU?
- **24 GB or more:** 1.0 to 1.4 MP.
- **16 GB:** 1.0 MP. Tested on an RTX 5070 Ti with 32 GB of system RAM.
- **12 GB:** switch on Low-VRAM mode in Render and use 0.7 MP. Not tested yet.
- Per segment, keep frames times megapixels under about 540.

The text encoder is NVFP4, which is built for RTX 50 cards. On an RTX 30 or 40 card, try `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot` from Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 instead. It's a bigger file, and it hasn't been tested here.

## Models
- **diffusion_models:** [Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_Pruned_v1.3_int8](https://huggingface.co/WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity)
- **text_encoders:** [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/text_encoders)
- **vae:** [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16 and minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/vae)
- **loras:** [minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/loras) and [h3-realism-people](https://huggingface.co/fal/MiniMax-H3-Realism-People-LoRA)
- **latent_upscale_models:** [3d_conv_v1_fp16](https://huggingface.co/LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler). Save it as `minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_fp16.safetensors`.
- **vae_approx:** [taeh3_2d_kijai](https://huggingface.co/t8star/Taeh3-Comfy). Save it as `taeh3.safetensors`.

## LoRAs
Singularity is a reference-to-video model. Keep the 4-step v0.1 turbo LoRA switched on with it, and don't swap in the 8-step one.

The realism LoRA runs at 0.5 for more natural people. Click it off to compare.

## Custom nodes
comfyui-easy-media, ComfyUI-KJNodes and rgthree-comfy. Install all three from ComfyUI Manager.

## Credits
Multi-track editor and project: comfyui-easy-media. Singularity fine-tune: WarmBloodAban. Realism LoRA: fal. Turbo LoRA and base files: Comfy-Org. Latent upscaler: LBH-123-AI. Preview model: t8star and Kijai.
